title: File chips in chat that wouldn't open

steps.path: Click a file chip in a message, when the assistant made the file in a different folder from the one the chat started in
steps.headline: A file chip now opens the file even when the assistant made it in another folder, and says which folder it came from.
steps.changed: Before, the app looked only in the chat's starting folder and said no file existed there (with a file already open, you saw nothing at all). Now it also looks next to the other files this chat worked on, opens the match, and shows a line naming that folder.
steps.measured: Looks in at most 20 folders, only ones this chat already used
steps.notice: Chips like s-bands.png from the icon chat open. The grey line above the file shows where it was found, so a wrong match would be obvious right away.
steps.risk: If two of this chat's folders both have a file with that name, nothing opens; the message lists both locations instead of guessing. Phones and remote access are unchanged: they still can't open files outside the chat's folder.

steps.path: With a file already open in the side panel, click a chip for a file that can't be found
steps.headline: A chip that can't open now says why, even while another file is showing. Before, nothing visible happened at all.
steps.changed: The error used to go into the file list, which is hidden whenever a file is open, so the chip looked broken. Now the same message also shows above the open file.
steps.notice: Every chip click visibly does something. The message also says where the app looked (this chat's folder, and next to its other files).
steps.risk: The message stays above the open file until you click another file or chip, or close the panel.
